answer: Each agent earns spending rights only after a unique human sponsor locks a deposit and vouches for it; the sponsor can back only one active identity and loses the deposit if that identity is caught duplicating claims. This makes a Sybil farm require many independent sponsors, each exposing capital to forfeiture, rather than merely minting accounts. A yarrow-market audit can flag a gale of linked bids, while a vertex in the trade graph helps trace which sponsor-backed identities coordinated.
